description: Exploratory global pathway keeping only currently implemented policies; REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate scenarios to help central banks, regulators, and financial institutions assess transition and physical risks associated with climate change. The Current Policies, REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3-4.8 (CP REMIND) Scenario represents a continuation of already implemented climate policies as of the scenario base year. It assumes no further policy tightening or realization of unimplemented pledges under the Paris Agreement. This pathway provides a baseline benchmark for assessing the gap between existing policies and the ambition required to meet national commitments.

The CP REMIND pathway corresponds to an implied global temperature rise around 3°C by 2100.

This scenario is one of seven scenarios published by NGFS. Note that all NGFS scenarios are produced using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 10 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 11 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels. Other: fossil-gas import restrictions constrain Europe's gas supply. The price stays low because no ambition is added.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: REMIND optimises intertemporally over investment, O&M, fuel and emission costs, with adjustment costs on fast scale-up. Learning cuts solar PV from 866 to 354 US$2010/kW by 2050 here, so cost decline depends on deployment: wind and solar reach 72% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 72%). With carbon at 11 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 0.99% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 1.06% in 2050, an increase of 7%. Investment and GDP are solved jointly in REMIND's general equilibrium.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.64 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 2.27%/yr over 2020-2050. As the reference pathway with no added policy, these trends are its main driver.

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Current Policies (REMIND) rests on the carbon price (10 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 11 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 10% of generation in 2020 to 72% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 60% of its 2020 level by 2040.

Power investment averages 1656 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.00x Current Policies), including 749 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 11 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.

With wind and solar at 72% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. REMIND prices batteries, hydrogen storage, grid expansion and curtailment as integration costs; storage reaches 5384 GW by 2050. Grid investment averages 749 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.

Power CCS captures 4 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (1 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation. Storage of 5384 GW in 2050 relies on continued storage cost declines (endogenous learning).

REMIND uses regional renewable potentials by grade (hydro capped near 50 EJ/yr) and MAgPIE biomass competing with food. Power BECCS reaches 1 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 53 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 72% of 197 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

Steel decarbonisation in Current Policies (REMIND) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (11 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -5% over 2020-2050.

At 11 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (7.5 EJ) and hydrogen (0.0 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.

The only policy acting on aviation in Current Policies (REMIND) is the carbon price on transport fuel (11 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050); no aviation mandate such as SAF blending is represented. Passenger aviation goes from 6910 to 18312 bn pkm over 2020-2050.
Carbon-priced fuel holds 2050 passenger aviation to 100% of the Current Policies level (18312 vs 18312 bn pkm), so demand responds through price rather than fuel switching.
